name: Numerical Sequence (easy version)
description: The only difference between the easy and the hard versions is the maximum value of $$$k$$$ . You are given an infinite sequence of form " 112123123412345$$$\dots$$$ " which consist of blocks of all consecutive positive integers written one after another. The first block consists of all numbers from $$$1$$$ to $$$1$$$, the second one — from $$$1$$$ to $$$2$$$, the third one — from $$$1$$$ to $$$3$$$, $$$\dots$$$, the $$$i$$$-th block consists of all numbers from $$$1$$$ to $$$i$$$. So the first $$$56$$$ elements of the sequence are " 11212312341234512345612345671234567812345678912345678910 ". Elements of the sequence are numbered from one. For example, the $$$1$$$-st element of the sequence is $$$1$$$, the $$$3$$$-rd element of the sequence is $$$2$$$, the $$$20$$$-th element of the sequence is $$$5$$$, the $$$38$$$-th element is $$$2$$$, the $$$56$$$-th element of the sequence is $$$0$$$. Your task is to answer $$$q$$$ independent queries. In the $$$i$$$-th query you are given one integer $$$k_i$$$. Calculate the digit at the position $$$k_i$$$ of the sequence.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le q \le 500$$$) — the number of queries. The $$$i$$$-th of the following $$$q$$$ lines contains one integer $$$k_i$$$ $$$(1 \le k_i \le 10^9)$$$ — the description of the corresponding query.
output_specification: Print $$$q$$$ lines. In the $$$i$$$-th line print one digit $$$x_i$$$ $$$(0 \le x_i \le 9)$$$ — the answer to the query $$$i$$$, i.e. $$$x_i$$$ should be equal to the element at the position $$$k_i$$$ of the sequence.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1216E1 — Numerical Sequence (easy version) [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
